_PROJECT_HOOK: ===== PROJECT HOOK: regenerate this ABI from THIS project's device profiler source =====
_how_to_fill: This example is deliberately tiny and generic. Replace it with the real ABI produced by your project's `extract_abi.py --write` (see examples/host/extract_abi.py). Keep the schema and section names; fill source_file/source_sha256/tasks/tracks/tag_bitfields to match YOUR device writer. decode_profile.py checks source_sha256 against the on-disk source, so a stale/placeholder ABI FAILS LOUDLY via the `abi_source_sha256_mismatch` diagnostic instead of silently decoding garbage.

buffer.zero_init_rationale: unwritten record slots are only recognizable because both elements stay 0
buffer.slot_formula: slot = (block * num_tracks * max_records + track * max_records + offset) * 2

block_map.purpose: logical CTA -> physical SM id mapping

layout.slot_formula: slot = (block * num_tracks * max_records + track * max_records + offset) * 2

block.meaning: blockIdx.x of the recording persistent CTA

enum.name: ExampleProfileTask
enum._count_note: count MUST equal len(tasks[]) — it is the device enum's cardinality, not a decoration. If you add/remove an event id, update it here too.

_tasks_hook: ===== PROJECT HOOK: one entry per real event id. `layer` is MANDATORY on every entry and must be exactly one of task|phase|ignored — decode_profile.py and emit_perfetto.py both refuse to default it, because the old default was "task" and that is what silently rendered a whole-core anchor as a full-width bar. Phase entries must carry parent_task_id (or parent_resolution="runtime_nesting" when the parent is only known by interval containment). emit_perfetto.py renders tasks as outer slices, phases nested inside their parent task on the same warp lane, and drops ignored entirely. =====

_layer_semantics._read_this_before_labelling: layer is not bookkeeping: it decides what gets drawn AND what counts in the operator-coverage numerator. A wrong label in the 'ignored' direction produces a wrong delivered number that every gate still passes.
_layer_semantics.task: A real operator interval. Rendered as an outer slice and counted toward operator coverage. Only use it for intervals whose duration you would quote as 'time spent in operator X'.
_layer_semantics.phase: A sub-interval strictly INSIDE one task (load / mma / epilogue / barrier / store ...). Rendered nested inside its parent task on the same warp lane, and collapsed away completely for a task-only delivery. Never counts as operator coverage by itself, and a phase span must never be used as the coverage envelope.
_layer_semantics.ignored: Recorded on device, decoded, and kept in events_rank*.json — but NEVER rendered as a span and NEVER counted as coverage. This is where whole-core markers belong: the kernel-wide entry/exit rendezvous named by sync_anchors.entry_rendezvous, and every grid_barrier / grid_sync boundary. They are kept because SW/HW alignment and cross-rank alignment are computed from them; they are not operators.
_layer_semantics._real_incident_this_prevents: A shipped delivery had the whole-core kernel anchor labelled layer="task". Because it spans the entire kernel it was drawn as one full-width bar on EVERY warp lane, which pushed the coverage envelope to 100%. That hid the actual shape of the run — only the attention stretch was really an operator, with a 769us head and a 337us tail containing no operator at all — and all 25 gates reported PASS. The true operator coverage was 44.9%.
_layer_semantics._how_to_decide_each_id: (1) Would you quote its duration as operator time? -> task. (2) Is it strictly contained in exactly one task? -> phase (set parent_task_id). (3) Is it a whole-core rendezvous / grid barrier / kernel-lifetime marker? -> ignored. Then VERIFY against a real decode: sum the per-lane span of every task-layer id; any id whose span approaches the kernel makespan on every lane is mislabelled and belongs in ignored.
_layer_semantics._do_not: Do not delete a whole-core anchor to keep it out of the picture — SW/HW alignment needs it. Mark it ignored so it stays in the decoded data and out of the render.

tasks.name: example_entry_sync
tasks.layer_note: Whole-core entry rendezvous = the SW/HW and cross-rank alignment zero. MUST stay layer="ignored": it spans the whole kernel, so rendering it would draw a full-width bar on every lane and fake 100% coverage. It is still decoded, and build_anchors()/align_sw_hw.py read it from here.

tasks.name: example_grid_barrier
tasks.layer_note: grid_sync boundary between operators: recorded for SW/HW diagnostics, never rendered, never counted as operator time. If your kernel has no grid barrier, delete this entry — do NOT relabel it as a task or a phase to 'fill the timeline'.

_tracks_hook: ===== PROJECT HOOK: one entry per observer track that actually records. role labels the warp's job; may_be_empty marks optionally-idle tracks =====

entry_rendezvous.alignment_usage: cross-rank + SW/HW baseline: entry_release is the common execution zero
entry_rendezvous.required_layer_rationale: The task named here spans the whole kernel on every CTA. It must be layer="ignored" in tasks[] so decode keeps it (alignment reads it) while emit_perfetto.py never draws it. Labelling it "task" is the exact mistake that produced a full-width bar on every lane and a fake 100% coverage envelope.

decoder_hints.stop_condition: first slot with timestamp_ns == 0 and tag == 0 terminates the track
decoder_hints.pairing: stack per task_id inside one (block, track); nesting of different tasks is expected
decoder_hints.truncation_check: records == max_records means events may be missing
decoder_hints.consistency_check: tag.block / tag.track must equal the block / track implied by the slot index
decoder_hints.empty_tracks_are_legal: PER-TRACK ONLY, never globally: a track may record nothing if and only if its tracks[] entry sets may_be_empty=true. decode_profile.py fails when a track declared may_be_empty=false recorded zero records, because a silently empty lane means that observer warp never fired — one whole warp of the delivery would be missing while every count still looked self-consistent. Decide may_be_empty per track from the reference config, do not blanket-allow emptiness.
